Hands-on training for public health laboratories

Bioinformatics Training Course

This course takes you from your first terminal command to inspecting real sequencing reads. Each section pairs a short lecture with hands-on activities you complete step by step at your own computer, with questions along the way to check your understanding.

No prior programming experience is needed — just a computer with a terminal.

Start the course ›See all sections Resume where you left off

Course sections

01 Foundations of Microbial Population Genomics Microbial evolution, mutation, recombination, population structure, genetic diversity, and species delineation. 0 lectures · 0 activities 02 Taxonomic Classification and Genomic Subtyping Genome-based species identification, MLST, k-mer-based methods, and other microbial typing approaches. 3 lectures · 3 activities 03 High-Resolution Genomic Relatedness Core genome MLST (cgMLST), core-SNP analysis, genomic distance, clustering, and analytical limitations. 0 lectures · 0 activities 04 Phylogenetic Methods and Tree Building Evolutionary models, tree-building methods, rooting, branch lengths, support values, and tree interpretation. 0 lectures · 0 activities 05 Interpreting Phylogenomic Evidence in Outbreak Investigations Genomic clusters, background diversity, epidemiological integration, uncertainty, and transmission inference limitations. 0 lectures · 0 activities 06 Integrated Genomic Epidemiology Case Studies Applying typing, genomic relatedness, phylogenetics, and epidemiological evidence to outbreak investigation scenarios. 0 lectures · 0 activities
